question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{2},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{4{x}^{3}},\, & 1<x<3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{9}{4{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{9}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{9}{4}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{4}-{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{4}-\frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-1).\end{aligned}
$$
